correctness.rationale: Exactly enumerating AB,BA vs AA,AB,BA,BB yields Qrr=(AB^2A+BA^2B)/2 and Qi=(A^4+B^4+AB^2A+BA^2B)/4. Writing A=I-omega uu^T, B=I-omega vv^T and using projector idempotence gives the operator identity in RESULT.md. Orthogonal bisectors have eigenvalues omega^2(2-omega)(1-c^2)[2-omega(1+/-c)]/4, with zero on the common orthogonal complement. Since 0<omega<2 and 0<c<1, the minus-bisector eigenvalue is positive and the plus-bisector eigenvalue changes sign only at 2/(1+c). This establishes all universal statements analytically. The 3-node path has inner product 1/2, giving threshold 4/3 and exact rational witnesses at omega=3/2. The extracted verifier passed 45 exact checks; finite tests are not used as a proof of universal signs. Reflection endpoint omega=2 is excluded and has zero difference.

value.rationale: The sharp pointwise sign law distinguishes energy savings from avoiding repeated edge selections and possible harm from overrelaxed, though individually nonexpansive, updates. On the smallest connected graph the nontrivial threshold 4/3 produces two explicit opposite initial-direction rankings at the same communication cost and marginals. It is a motivated structural benchmark for gossip and row-action sampling, rather than a bare normalization check or arbitrary finite statistic. The narrow two-step theorem is useful as a boundary for stronger, unjustified claims about uniformly beneficial reshuffling; no multiepoch theorem is claimed.
